newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, gold near 4 year low.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, gold near 4 year low.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower across the board Wednesday, with gold slipping to near four-year lows on news of more European central bank gold sales, and platinum group metals lower as the date for the resumption of Russian exports draws nearer.

"The Belgian plan to sell more gold via a bullion coin issue still needs parliamentary approval and will not impact until 1999, but the market just saw it as more evidence of a trend toward central bank gold sales and ended weaker," said Ted Kempf, an analyst with industry consultants CPM Group in New York.
COMEX August gold ended down $2.80 at $340290 an ounce, after seeing a new life-of-contract low at $340.60, with contract lows also being seen in the December 1997 and February 1998 delivery months.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $338.90/40, not far from the four year low around $336.15 seen on February 15 this year.

Belgian central bank officials said Wednesday the Belgian government proposed increasing the amount of central bank gold that can be sold as commemorative gold coins to 26 tonnes a year from 1999 onwards, up to a maximum of 133 tonnes.

Currently the National Bank of Belgium is authorized to sell up to 2.75 percent of its 1987 gold reserves in the form of coins, and the new proposal is to increase the amount authorized to 10 percent of the 1987 reserves.
At the start of 1987 the Belgian central bank held 1,329 tonnes of gold, but had sold 733 tonnes by the end of 1996.
The proposed extra sales of coins would allow Belgium to pay down more of its debt which stands at 129 pct of GDP, the highest debt-to-GDP ratio in the EU.
But the plan must still obtain parliamentary approval and would also be subject to approval by the new European Central Bank (ECB) which is due to be operational from January 1999.

"I dont believe the Belgian government will be able to sell that amount of gold in commemorative coins," said Leonard Kaplan, a broker with MONEX, one of the largest U.S. retailers of gold investment products.

Total world sales of major bullion coins (Krugerrand, American Eagle, Austrian Philharmonic, Canadian Maple Leaf, Australian Nugget, English Britannia) in 1996 amounted to 36.8 tonnes, according to the latest World Gold Council survey.
"But central banks are looking for a method of disposing of more of their gold reserves, so this kind of thing will only happen more often," Kaplan said.

The move by the Belgian government came only two days after Jean-Pierre Patat, an official of France's central bank, told the Financial Times gold conference in Prague that several European central banks which had sold gold from their reserves now feel there is no longer an advantage in doing so.
Belgium last sold a significant quantity of its reserves in March 1996 when it announced a sale of 203 tonnes.
On another negative note, the Swiss parliament Wednesday approved a revised charter for the Swiss central bank, allowing it to start lending gold to improve its earnings.
The charter also reduced the amount of gold the Swiss National Bank must hold to cover its notes in circulation to 25 percent from 40 percent.
COMEX July silver ended down 6.7 cents at $4.695 an ounce, reversing Tuesday's gains.
July silver has been in a $4.65-4.90 range since mid-May, with good industrial demand seen below $4.70 and ample supply seen near $4.90, analysts said.
NYMEX July platinum ended down $4.20 at $406.90 an ounce.

July platinum has now closed down seven times in the past eight days, retreating from a contract high at $473.80, as funds continue to liquidate long positions ahead of the contract's delivery period starting in two weeks.
Open interest in July platinum fell a further 830 lots Tuesday to 9,615 lots representing 480,750 ounces, while NYMEX warehouse platinum stocks were unchanged at 54,700 ounces.
NYMEX September palladium ended down $8.45 at $169.45, after execution of a large stop order at $170.00, traders said.
But in the physical market, one month lease rates for platinum remained around 50 percent and for palladium around 100 percent, while the market waited for Russian supplies resume in late June.

In overnight news, the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said it was in discussions with the London Platinum and Palladium Market Association about restoring orderly trading conditions to the PGM market.
The London Platinum and Palladium Market had also contacted the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), TOCOM officials said.
